rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gayy lexically means bad, troublesome, rebellious, or astray; the author prefers the metaphorical rendering punishment for their transgression.
rows.anchor: gayy kelimesi sözlükte, “kötü, yaramaz, azgın ve sapmış” anlamlarında kullanılmaktadır, biz “azgınlıklarının cezası” şeklindeki mecaz anlamını tercih ettik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gayy is also reported to be the name of a valley in Hell.
rows.anchor: Gayy kelimesinin Cehennemdeki bir vadinin ismi olduğu rivayeti de vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer, in differing forms, was prescribed for every prophet and community because it draws a servant near to God, connects the servant with Him, and protects from evil.
rows.anchor: Şekli farklı da olsa namaz bütün peygamberlere ve ümmetlerine farz kılınmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Later generations after earlier prophets either abandoned prayer or neglected its required elements; weakening their bond with God let carnal desires dominate and displaced divine commands with personal wishes.
rows.anchor: eski peygamberlerden sonra gelenler namazı ya hiç kılmamışlar veya onun edasında yerine getirilmesi gereken hususlara dikkat etmemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse warns that these people will not escape consequences and will certainly receive punishment.
rows.anchor: Âyet, bunların yaptıklarının karşılıksız kalmayacağını, cezalarını mutlaka çekeceklerini ifade etmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No sin is beyond repentance; sincere repentance joined with faith, worship, good conduct, and genuine turning to God makes believers worthy of His promise of Paradise.
rows.anchor: İnsanların günahları ne olursa olsun tövbenin silemeyeceği günah yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adn is an exceptional part of Paradise reserved for the closest and most select servants: prophets, martyrs, the truthful, and scholars.
rows.anchor: Adn, cennetin müstesna bölümlerinden biri olup oranın, mukarrebûn denilen ve peygamberler, şehidler, sıddîklar ve âlimlerden oluşan Allah’ın en seçkin kullarına tahsis edildiği bildirilmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise's believers hear no speech that brings fear or anxiety; they remain happy and secure, continually hearing salām as glad tidings of new joys.
rows.anchor: orada korku ve endişeye kapılacak bir söz işitmeyecekler, hep mutluluk ve esenlik içinde olacak

rows.speaker: Abdullah b. Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet asked Gabriel to visit him more often, and these verses were revealed in response.
rows.anchor: Abdullah b. Abbas’tan rivayet edildiğine göre Resulullah, Cebrâil’in kendisini daha çok ziyaret etmesini istemiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Quraysh questioned the Prophet, he promised a near answer, and when Gabriel was delayed they claimed his Lord had forgotten him; the Prophet grieved and these verses followed.
rows.anchor: inkârcılar Hz. Peygamber’e bazı konularda sorular sormuşlar; Peygamber efendimiz de kendilerine yakında bilgi vereceğini söylemiş

rows.speaker: Müfessirlerin genel kabulü
rows.claim: The prevailing exegetical view is that these are God's words, commanding Gabriel to answer the Prophet accordingly.
rows.anchor: Müfessirlerin genel kabulüne göre bu iki âyet Allah’ın sözü olup Cebrâil’e, Hz. Peygamber’e böyle cevap vermesini emretmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The free rendering says angels descend only at their Lord's command; all places and times belong to God, and delayed revelation reflects wisdom rather than forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: Onun emri ve iradesi olmadan biz hiçbir zaman ve hiçbir yerde hareket edemeyiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Semiyy can mean similar, but the author prefers worthy to bear His name: Arabs reserved the name Allah for God and called idols ilāh.
rows.anchor: “Adını almaya lâyık” diye çevirdiğimiz semiyy kelimesi, “benzer” mânasına da gelir. Bizim de tercih ettiğimiz birinci mânaya göre Allah ismi, yüce yaratıcı olan Cenâb-ı Hak’tan başkasına verilmemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the alternative meaning of semiyy as similar, the verse denies that God has any equal and therefore denies that anything besides Him deserves worship.
rows.anchor: İkinci mânaya göre âyet, Allah’ın eşi ve benzerinin bulunmadığını, dolayısıyla ondan başka hiçbir şeyin ibadet edilmeye lâyık olmadığını belirtir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering creation from nothing shows that the power that first created a person can raise that person after death and decay; other verses likewise say resurrection repeats the first creation and is easier for God.
rows.anchor: Oysa insan ilk yaratılışını düşünürse kendisini yoktan var eden bir kudretin

rows.speaker: Şevkânî
rows.claim: The devils here are unbelieving leaders who deceive people by denying a Hereafter, accountability, and any life beyond this world.
rows.anchor: 68. âyetteki “şeytanlar”dan maksat insanların ilâhî huzura çıkıp dünyada yaptıklarından hesaba çekilecekleri bir âhiret günü olmadığını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will gather those leaders and the people they misled at the assembly and punish them.
rows.anchor: Yüce Allah, bunları ve bunların kandırarak yoldan çıkardığı kimseleri mahşerde toplayıp cezalarını vereceğini buyurmuştur

rows.speaker: bazı tefsirciler
rows.claim: Some exegetes say the rebellious will be sorted out: the most sinful enter Hell, while those whose rebellion is lighter may be forgiven.
rows.anchor: İsyankârların bir kısmı ayırt edilip cehenneme atılacak, isyanı daha hafif olanlar ise bağışlanacaklar

rows.speaker: tefsircilerin çoğunluğu
rows.claim: Most exegetes take the verse as wholly about unbelievers: they are divided by degrees of disbelief and rebellion into corresponding levels of Hell, with leading instigators punished more severely.
rows.anchor: tefsircilerin çoğunluğuna göre âyet bütünüyle kâfirlere dairdir. Ayırt edilmekten maksat ise insanların inkârcılık ve isyan derecesine göre çeşitli gruplara ayrılmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows exactly who is most rebellious and applies each person's deserved punishment according to the degree of sin, with perfect justice.
rows.anchor: kimlerin daha fazla isyankâr olduğunu eksiksiz bilen Allah Teâlâ, herkese, isyan ve günahlarının derecesine göre hak ettiği cezayı da eksiksiz bilecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes the universal arrival at Hell to mean that everyone crosses the bridge over it; the God-fearing are spared from Hell, while wrongdoers remain there kneeling.
rows.anchor: Bunlardan maksat sırattan geçenlerdir. Mümin olsun kâfir olsun bütün insanlar aynı zamanda cehennemin üstünde kurulmuş olan sırattan geçmek zorunda

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes those addressed as the unbelievers, who will enter Hell.
rows.anchor: Maksat kâfirlerdir ve bunlar cehenneme gireceklerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation says every person is potentially bound for either Paradise or Hell according to deeds.
rows.anchor: Potansiyel olarak her insan ameline göre cennete olduğu kadar cehenneme de girebilecek durumdadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets' earliest followers are often poor and weak, while wealthy and powerful rejecters belittle and oppress them; the Qur'an gives many examples.
rows.anchor: Genellikle peygamberlere ilk inananlar toplumun zayıfları ve fakirleridir. Onları inkâr edenler ise servet ve iktidar sahipleridir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arrogant Quraysh argued that a good message would have come to them instead of the poor, and asked which camp had superior status, followers, and homes.
rows.anchor: “Eğer bu iyi bir şey olsaydı bizi bırakıp da onlara gelmezdi!” (Ahkaf 46/11) diyerek kendilerinin daha üstün

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists demanded that the Prophet drive away the poor before they would listen to his message.
rows.anchor: ancak fakirleri yanından kovduğu takdirde Hz. Peygamber’in tebliğini dinleyebileceklerini bildirmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse recalls prosperous peoples such as ʿĀd and Thamūd, who cultivated land and built thriving countries but were destroyed for disbelief, urging the arrogant to learn from their remains.
rows.anchor: Âd ve Semûd gibi eski kavimlerin akıbetleri hatırlatılarak onların kalıntılarına bakıp ibret almaları tavsiye edilmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat answers the boast in verse 73: children, power, and wealth are not necessarily gifts but may be istidrāj, a respite that lets the arrogant persist in evil before punishment.
rows.anchor: müşriklere vermiş olduğu evlât, devlet ve servetin gerçekte bir lutuf olmadığını, onlara bu nimetlerin verilmesinin bir istidrâc olduğunu ifade etmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Increasing or sustaining blessings used for good is grace; giving a boastful wrongdoer further time and opportunity is istidrāj.
rows.anchor: Kul, Allah’ın vermiş olduğu nimeti hayırlı işlerde kullanıyorsa bu nimetin arttırılması, sürekli kılınması bir lutuftur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihtadaw derives from huda, meaning finding or showing the right path; ihtidā means finding truth, and technically means adopting Islam from unbelief or another religion, with such a convert called a muhtadī.
rows.anchor: Bu fiilin masdarı olan ihtidâ ise “doğru yolu bulmak, gerçeğe ulaşmak” anlamlarına gelmektedir. Terim olarak inançsız iken veya başka bir dine mensupken İslâm dinini benimsemeyi ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda occurs 85 times in the Qur'an and means guidance; exegetes and theologians assign contextual senses, while Raghib defines hidaya as gracious direction.
rows.anchor: Kur’an’da seksen beş yerde geçen hüdâ kelimesi ise sözlükte “yol göstermek, kılavuzluk etmek” anlamına gelmektedir. Müfessir ve kelâmcılar hüdâ kelimesine bağlamına göre çeşitli mânalar vermişlerdir

rows.speaker: Râgıb el-İsfahânî
rows.claim: Raghib groups divine guidance into four linked stages: necessary reason-based knowledge, prophetic and revelatory invitation, enabling guidance for those who accept, and Paradise as their afterlife reward.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın insanlara olan hidayeti dört merhaleden oluşur: 1. Her mükellefe lutfettiği akıl ve idrak yetenekleriyle hayatını sürdürmeyi sağlayan zaruri bilgiler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four forms depend on one another in sequence: each earlier form must occur for the next guidance to be realized.
rows.anchor: Bu hidayet türleri buradaki tertibe göre birbirine bağlı olup bir sonraki hidayetin gerçekleşmesi için bir öncekinin meydana gelmesi şarttır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's increase of guidance means the third and fourth stages: someone who chooses the right path through reason and will is enabled to persevere and ultimately rewarded with Paradise.
rows.anchor: cümleden kastedilen mâna 3 ve 4. merhaledeki anlamlardır. Buna göre bir kimse aklını ve iradesini kullanarak doğru yola girerse Allah ona o yolda yürüyüp başarıya ulaşmayı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward of good deeds with God exceeds worldly things people boast about, because good deeds accompany their owner into the Hereafter and benefit them eternally.
rows.anchor: Hayırlı davranışların Allah katındaki sevabı, yeryüzündekilerin iftihar ettikleri her şeyden daha üstün ve sonuç itibariyle daha iyidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported occasion concerns the poor Muslim blacksmith Khabbāb, who demanded his debt from al-ʿĀṣ b. Wāʾil; al-ʿĀṣ refused repayment unless Khabbāb rejected Muhammad.
rows.anchor: Fakir bir müslüman olup Mekke’de demircilikle meşgul olan Habbâb b. Eret’in, yaptığı bir işten dolayı müşriklerin ileri gelenlerinden Âs b. Vâil’de alacağı vardı

rows.speaker: Habbâb b. Eret
rows.claim: Khabbāb swore he would never reject Muhammad even until al-ʿĀṣ died and was raised; al-ʿĀṣ claimed he would have wealth and children then and repay him.
rows.anchor: “Allah’a yemin ederim ki sen ölüp tekrar dirilinceye kadar onu asla inkâr etmem” dedi. Âs, “Gerçekten ben ölüp tekrar dirilecek miyim?” diye sordu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheists sought help, honor, and prestige from their deities because each tribe's idol also symbolized its standing.
rows.anchor: Müşrikler Allah’tan başka taptıkları ilâhlardan yardım bekliyor ve bundan izzet ve şeref umuyorlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation predicts that paganism would end in the Prophet's community as polytheists became Muslims, rejected false gods, and opposed them; verses about their later denial support this reading.
rows.anchor: bir süre sonra müşriklerin müslüman olup bâtıl ilâhlara ibadeti reddedeceklerini ve onlara düşman olacaklarını müjdelemektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading places the event on Judgment Day, when the deities themselves repudiate their worshippers and become their enemies; the author prefers this interpretation.
rows.anchor: Kıyamet gününde ilâhlar, kendilerine tapanların ibadetlerini reddedip onlara düşman olacaklardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that persistent disbelief and disobedience cause God to leave disbelievers unprotected from Satan.
rows.anchor: kâfirlerin inkâr ve isyanda direnmeleri sebebiyle Allah’ın onları şeytanlara karşı korumamasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God empowers devils over persistent rejecters; devils whisper and beautify evil until they commit it and enter Hell.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın, şeytanları inkârcıların üzerine musallat kılmasıdır. Kâfirler, inat ve ısrarla inkârlarını, Allah ve Peygamber’e karşı düşmanlıklarını sürdürürlerse Allah da onlara şeytanları musallat eder

rows.speaker: müfessirler
rows.claim: Exegetes identify what God counts as people's lifespans, which are fixed, limited, and known to Him; the verse tells the Prophet to be patient until their appointed destruction, many leaders having died at Badr.
rows.anchor: Müfessirlere göre “Allah’ın saydığı şey”den maksat insanların dünyadaki ömrüdür. Bu sebeple âyetin ilgili bölümü “Biz onların günlerini sayıyoruz” şeklinde tercüme edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing, who avoid disobedience and fulfill God's commands, gather before the Merciful for reward, while sinners are driven to Hell like a herd driven to water.
rows.anchor: takvâ sahipleri, yani Allah’a itaatsizlikten sakınıp buyruklarını yerine getirenler ödüllerine nâil olmak için rahmânın huzurunda toplanırken günahkârların da suya götürülen sürü gibi cehenneme sürüleceği bildirilmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading identifies those holding a covenant from the Merciful as people authorized to intercede in the Hereafter for those deserving it.
rows.anchor: Bunlar âhirette lâyık olanlara şefaat etmek için kendilerine izin verilenlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading identifies them as people whose faith and deeds in this world earn eligibility for intercession; those God permits will intercede for their sins to be forgiven.
rows.anchor: Dünyada iken şefaati hak ettiren iman ve amel sahibi olanlar. Bunlar Allah’ın birliği, peygamberlik, âhiret vb. iman esaslarına inandıkları için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheists called angels God's daughters, some Jews called Ezra His son, and Christians called the Messiah His son; verses 90–91 underscore the ugliness of these claims.
rows.anchor: Müşrikler, “Melekler Allah’ın kızlarıdır” diyerek Allah’a çocuk isnadında bulunurken yahudilerin bir kısmı “Üzeyir Allah’ın oğludur”, hıristiyanlar da “Mesîh Allah’ın oğludur” demek suretiyle O’na çocuk isnat ederek son derece çirkin bir iddiada bulunmuşlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Children are sought from need and belong to their parents' kind; God is exalted above both need and having any likeness.
rows.anchor: çocuk ihtiyaçtan dolayı istenir ve ana babasının cinsinden olur. Allah ise ihtiyaçtan da bir benzerinin bulunmasından da münezzehtir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created the heavens, earth, and all their inhabitants, including angels, jinn, and humans; they are servants, not deities, and obey and worship Him.
rows.anchor: Gökler, yer, bunların içinde bulunan melek, cin, insan vb. ne varsa hepsini Allah yaratmıştır; onlar tanrı değil Allah’ın kullarıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows those beings and those who attribute a child to Him, and knows their number and deeds.
rows.anchor: Allah, onlardan ve kendisine çocuk yakıştıranlardan haberdardır, onların sayılarını ve yaptıklarını bilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Resurrection everyone will gather individually before God and answer for their deeds alone.
rows.anchor: Kıyamet gününde herkes tek tek O’nun huzurunda toplanacak ve yaptıklarıyla başbaşa kalarak hesap vereceklerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent each prophet's message in the language of his people; the Arabic Qur'an was made understandable to the Arab Prophet so he could understand and clearly convey its good news and warnings.
rows.anchor: Kur’an’ı da Arap olan Hz. Peygamber’e Arapça olarak indirmek ve anlaşılır kılmak suretiyle kolaylaştırmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing verse warns that many earlier generations denied God's signs, ignored warnings, and were erased from earth and history; no sound or breath remains, and Quran's heedless rejecters will likewise be punished.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın âyetlerini inkâr edip uyarılarına kulak vermeyen nice nesillerin helâk edildiği, böylece onların yeryüzünden ve tarih sahnesinden silinip gittikleri bildirilmektedir

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: Saʿd reports that after the Qur'an had been recited to them for a time, listeners asked the Prophet to tell them something, prompting the revelation that God sent the best discourse.
rows.anchor: عن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال أنزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم القرآن فتلاه عليهم زمانا فقالوا يا رسول الله لو حدثتنا

rows.speaker: ابن أبي حاتم
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim adds that they asked the Prophet to remind them, prompting the verse asking whether believers' hearts should humble themselves to God's reminder.
rows.anchor: زاد ابن أبي حاتم فقالوا يا رسول الله لو ذكرتنا فأنزل الله ﴿ ألم يأن للذين آمنوا أن تخشع قلوبهم ﴾

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that they asked the Prophet to narrate stories, and this verse about the best of stories was revealed.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن عباس قال قالوا يا رسول الله لو قصصت علينا فنزل ﴿ نحن نقص عليك أحسن القصص ﴾

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud transmitted a similar report about the request for stories and revelation of this verse.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن ابن مسعود مثله

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: A weak report says Khadija asked about polytheists' children: the Prophet first said they followed their parents, later said God knows what they would have done, and after Islam strengthened said they are on the fitra or in Paradise.
rows.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن عائشة قالت سألت خديجة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أولاد المشركين

rows.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
rows.claim: When people of Muzayna asked the Prophet for transport and he had none, they left weeping, thinking he was angry; the verse about turning away while seeking God's mercy was revealed.
rows.anchor: أخرج سعيد بن منصور عن عطاء الخراساني قال جاء ناس من مزينة يستحملون رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the verse about turning away while seeking mercy was revealed concerning poor people who asked the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن الضحاك قال نزلت فيمن كان يسأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من المساكين

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Saʿid reports that after the verse giving a relative his due was revealed, the Prophet summoned Fatima and gave her Fadak.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال لما أنزلت ﴿ وآت ذا القربى حقه ﴾ دعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فاطمة فأعطاها فدك

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls this report problematic because it implies the verse is Medinan, contrary to the well-known view that it is Meccan; Ibn Mardawayh also reports it from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: قال ابن كثير هذا مشكل فانه يشعر بأن الآية مدنية والمشهور خلافه

rows.speaker: ابن شهاب
rows.claim: Ibn Shihab reports that Quraysh mocked the Prophet as he recited the Qur'an and invited them to the Book, claiming their hearts, ears, and the space between them were veiled; the verse followed.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن المنذر عن ابن شهاب قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا تلا القرآن على مشركي قريش ودعاهم إلى الكتاب قالوا يهزؤون به

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that some people worshipped jinn who later became Muslims while their human worshippers persisted, prompting the verse telling people to call on those they claim besides God.
rows.anchor: أخرج البخاري وغيره عن ابن مسعود قال كان ناس من الأنس يعبدون ناسا من الجن فأسلم الجنيون واستمسك الآخرون بعبادتهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Meccans asked for the Ṣafā to become gold and nearby mountains to move for farming; given the choice of granting their request or delaying, with destruction if they disbelieved, the Prophet chose delay.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال سأل أهل مكة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يجعل لهم الصفا ذهبا وان ينحي عنهم الجبال فيزرعوا

rows.speaker: الزبير
rows.claim: Al-Zubayr transmitted a similar, fuller account of the Meccans' request for signs.
rows.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني وابن مردويه منها عن الزبير نحوه أبسط منه

rows.speaker: أم هانىء
rows.claim: Umm Hani reports that Quraysh mocked the Prophet after the Night Journey, demanded a sign, and heard his description of Jerusalem and the caravan; al-Walid called him a magician, and the vision verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: أخرج أبو يعلي عن أم هانىء أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم لما أسري به أصبح يحدث نفرا من قريش يستهزؤون به فطلبوا منه آية

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reports that the Prophet awoke distressed; he was told not to grieve because his vision was a trial for them, and the verse followed.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن الحسن نحوه

rows.speaker: الحسين بن علي
rows.claim: Al-Husayn ibn Ali reports a similar account in which the Prophet was distressed and was comforted that his vision was a trial for them.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن الحسين بن علي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أصبح يوما مهموما فقيل له مالك يا رسول الله لا تهتم فإن رؤياك فتنة لهم

rows.speaker: سهل بن سعد
rows.claim: Sahl ibn Saʿd transmitted a similar report about the vision being a trial for them.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير من حديث سهل بن سعد نحوه

rows.speaker: عمرو بن العاص ويعلى بن مرة وسعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Related reports also came through ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, Yaʿlā ibn Murra, and the mursal Successor Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib, but their chains are weak.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم من حديث عمرو بن العاص ومن حديث يعلى بن مرة ومن مرسل سعيد بن المسيب نحوها وأسانيدها ضعيفة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Jahl mocked the warning about the Zaqqum tree, joking that it was bread with butter and boasting they would swallow it; the warning verses about the cursed tree and Zaqqum followed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال ذكر الله الزقوم خوف به هذا الحي من قريش قال أبو جهل هل تدرون ما هذا الزقوم الذي يخوفكم به محمد

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن غنم
rows.claim: A weak mursal report says Jews urged the Prophet to go to Syria, land of prophets and resurrection; he went toward it on the Tabuk campaign, but at Tabuk revelation ordered him back to Medina and taught him the prayer of 17:80.
rows.anchor: من حديث شهر بن حوشب عن عبد الرحمن بن غنم أن اليهود أتوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا ان كنت نبيا فالحق بالشام

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: A mursal corroboration says polytheists told the Prophet the prophets lived in Syria rather than Medina, and when he considered leaving this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وله شاهد من مرسل سعيد بن جبير عند ابن أبي حاتم ولفظه قالت المشركون للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كانت الأنبياء تسكن الشام فمالك والمدينة

rows.speaker: بعض اليهود
rows.claim: Another mursal route says that some Jews told the Prophet the same thing about Syria.
rows.anchor: وله طريق أخرى مرسلة عند ابن جرير ان بعض اليهود قاله له

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when the Prophet was in Mecca and then commanded to emigrate, the prayer for a truthful entrance and exit and supporting authority was revealed, explicitly showing the verse is Meccan.
rows.anchor: أخرج الترمذي عن ابن عباس قال كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة ثم أمر بالهجرة فنزلت عليه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that in Medina, while walking with the Prophet, Quraysh asked him about the Spirit; after a pause for revelation, he recited that the Spirit is from God's command.
rows.anchor: مسعود قال كنت أمشي مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالمدينة وهو متوكىء على عسيب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Quraysh asked Jews what to ask the Prophet, and they suggested the Spirit; the verse was revealed in answer.
rows.anchor: وأخرج الترمذي عن ابن عباس قال قالت قريش لليهود علمونا شيئا نسأل هذا الرجل فقالوا سلوه عن الروح

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وابن حجر
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Ibn Hajar reconcile the two Spirit reports by repeated revelation; Ibn Hajar also suggests the Prophet's silence anticipated further clarification, while Suyuti prefers Ibn Masʿud's firsthand report as more reliable than Ibn Abbas's.
rows.anchor: قلت ويرجح ما في الصحيح بأن راوية حاضر القصة بخلاف ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Ibn Mishkam and Jewish companions challenged the Prophet to provide a recognizable book or they would produce one like the Qur'an; the Qur'an's inimitability verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: من طريق سعيد أو عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ابن مشكم في عامة من يهود سماهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Quraysh leaders demanded money, status, removal of mountains, rivers, resurrected ancestors, an angel, wealth, or a heavenly ladder with witnesses; after the Prophet refused, the demand for signs in these verses was revealed.
rows.anchor: اجتمعوا فقالوا يا محمد ما نعلم رجلا من العرب أدخل على قومه ما أدخلت على قومك لقد سببت الآباء وعبت الدين

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the demand for signs was revealed about Umm Salama's brother, ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Umayya; this sound mursal report corroborates and clarifies the preceding report's unnamed figure.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله ﴿ وقالوا لن نؤمن لك ﴾ قال نزلت في أخي أم سلمة عبد الله بن أبي أمية مرسل صحيح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when the Prophet prayed in Mecca and invoked Allah and al-Rahman, polytheists mocked him for supposedly calling two gods, prompting the verse permitting either name.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة ذات يوم فدعا فقال في دعائه يا الله يا رحمن فقال المشركون انظروا إلى هذا الصابىء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that while secretly in Mecca the Prophet recited aloud in prayer; polytheists insulted the Qur'an, its revealer, and its bearer, prompting the instruction not to recite too loudly or too quietly.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله ﴿ ولا تجهر بصلاتك ولا تخافت بها ﴾ قال نزلت ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مختف بمكة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the instruction not to recite too loudly or quietly concerned supplication; Ibn Jarir also transmits a similar report from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: وأخرج البخاري أيضا عن عائشة أنها نزلت في الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suyuti and Nawawi prefer the first, stronger-chain explanation; Ibn Hajar says both can be reconciled if the supplication occurred inside prayer, supported by a report from Abu Hurayra about prayer at the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: ثم رجح الأولى لكونها أصح سندا وكذا رجحها النووي وغيره وقال الحافظ ابن حجر لكن يحتمل الجمع بينهما بأنها نزلت في الدعاء داخل الصلاة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the verse concerned the tashahhud, clarifying her earlier report about supplication.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير والحاكم عن عائشة قالت نزلت هذه الآية في التشهد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that people used to loudly pray for mercy, so they were ordered neither to whisper nor to raise their voices.
rows.anchor: ولابن منيع في مسنده عن ابن عباس كانوا يجهرون بالدعاء اللهم ارحمني فنزلت فأمروا أن لا يخافتوا ولا يجهروا

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb reports that Jews, Christians, Arabs, Sabians, and Magi made claims about divine offspring, partners, or protectors, prompting the verse praising God as free of a child, partner, or humiliating ally.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير عن محمد بن كعب القرظي قال إن اليهود والنصارى قالوا اتخذ الله ولدا وقالت العرب لبيك لا شريك لك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Quraysh sent two men to Jewish scholars, who proposed questions about ancient youths, a world traveler, and the Spirit; after the Prophet promised an answer without saying God willing, revelation paused fifteen nights, then the Cave chapter came with a rebuke for grieving over rejecters.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال بعثت قريش النضر بن الحرث وعقبة بن أبي معيط إلى أحبار اليهود بالمدينة فقالوا لهم سلوهم عن محمد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another Ibn Abbas report says Quraysh leaders' rejection of the Prophet's counsel grieved him greatly, and this verse about his sorrow was revealed.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن ابن عباس قال اجتمع عتبة بن ربيعة وشيبة ابن ربيعة وأبو جهل بن هشام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that after people asked whether the Cave-dwellers' three hundred years meant years or months, the verse adding nine was revealed; al-Dahhak also transmitted it.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه أيضا عن ابن عباس قال أنزلت ﴿ ولبثوا في كهفهم ثلاث مائة ﴾ فقيل يا رسول الله سنين أو شهورا فأنزل الله ﴿ سنين وازدادوا تسعا ﴾

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that forty nights after the Prophet swore an oath, the instruction not to promise future action without God's will was revealed.
rows.anchor: وأخرجه ابن جرير عن الضحاك وأخرجه ابن مردويه أيضا عن أبن عباس قال حلف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على يمين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Quraysh asked Jews what to ask the Prophet; after the Spirit verse, Jews boasted of their Torah knowledge, and the verse comparing God's words to an endless sea was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال قالت قريش لليهود أعطونا شيئا نسأل عنه هذا الرجل فقالوا سلوه عن الروح

rows.speaker: طاوس
rows.claim: Tawus reports that a man said he acted for God's sake but liked others to see his standing; the Prophet gave no reply until this verse was revealed. Al-Hakim transmitted it connected through Ibn Abbas and authenticated it to the standards of the two Ṣaḥīḥs.
rows.anchor: عن طاوس قال قال رجل يا رسول الله إني أقف أريد وجه الله وأحب أن يرى موطني فلم يرد عليه شيئا حتى نزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reports that a Muslim fighting in battle liked people to see where he stood, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن مجاهد كان رجل من المسلمين يقاتل وهو يحب أن يرى مكانه

rows.speaker: جندب بن زهير
rows.claim: Jundub ibn Zuhayr reports that a man increased prayer, fasting, and charity when praised by people, prompting this verse about pure worship.
rows.anchor: قال جندب بن زهير إذا صلى الرجل أو صام أو تصدق فذكر بخير ارتاح له فزاد في ذلك لمقالة الناس له

rows.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
rows.claim: Khabbāb reports that al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil withheld his debt unless Khabbāb disbelieved in Muhammad; when Khabbāb refused until after his death and resurrection, al-ʿĀṣ boasted he would have wealth and children there, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن خباب بن الأرت قال جئت العاصي بن وائل السهمي أتقاضاه حقا لي عنده فقال لا أعطينك حتى تكفر بمحمد
